title: A Protocol for the Gravity Again
premise: Theo Thornbury investigates impossible accidents for the Interworld Insurance Consortium, the only institution still trusted by two star systems that severed contact after a war both claim the other started. When a name appears on the manifest of a ship that officially never flew, Theo traces it to a survivor carrying proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged — and that Theo's own employer helped stage it. Pursued by Consortium enforcers and haunted by a partner they were forced to disavow, Theo must deliver the truth to both capitals before a scheduled ceasefire expires. In the end, Theo broadcasts the evidence from neutral space, sacrificing their career and their last chance at reinstatement, but forcing both worlds to face a shared lie — and giving them a reason to speak again.
about_author: Bram Vasquez is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years reconstructing disasters nobody wanted explained. They write in the long silences between shipping lanes, where every accident has an author.

chapters.title: The Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Theo Thornbury, investigating a docking-crane collapse on the neutral station Vespergate, finds an impossible entry: a passenger listed aboard the Meridian Lark, a vessel stricken from all records after the war's first battle. The emotional beat is quiet unease — Theo's professional instinct that something is wrong before anything proves it. POV: Theo, close third.

chapters.title: A Name Out of Water
chapters.summary: Theo tracks the manifest name to Ilsa Reyes, a hydroponics tech living under a dead sister's identity. She claims she was crew on the Meridian Lark and survived its destruction — an event both governments insist never happened. Her fear is contagious; someone has already searched her quarters. POV: Theo, with Ilsa's testimony as embedded account. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Consortium Paid For
chapters.summary: Digging through archived claims, Theo discovers the Consortium insured the Meridian Lark twice — once as destroyed, once as decommissioned — and paid out on both. The contradiction points to a staged atrocity used to justify the war. POV: Theo. Beat: the sick vertigo of realizing your employer is the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Theo and Ilsa book passage on a slow freighter along the lawless long route between the two hostile systems, hoping to reach an archivist who can authenticate the manifests. Enforcers board at a fueling relay; the pair barely slip away through cargo bays. POV: alternating Theo and Ilsa. Beat: loyalty tested — Ilsa asks why Theo is helping, and Theo has no honest answer yet.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Broken Records
chapters.summary: In a drifting archive hulk, blind archivist Sef Oduya confirms the double payout but reveals worse: the atrocity footage was manufactured, and the Consortium holds the original unedited files. He gives them a decryption key and a warning — the ceasefire talks expire in nineteen days. POV: Theo. Beat: hope arriving tangled with a deadline.

chapters.title: Everything Theo Signed
chapters.summary: Consortium enforcers capture Ilsa, and Theo learns their former partner, Wren Calloway, now leads the hunt — and that Theo's own past investigations buried evidence of the staging. Confronted via transmission, Wren offers Theo reinstatement if they walk away. POV: Theo. Beat: shame and temptation; the theme of loyalty versus truth turns inward.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Then Nine
chapters.summary: Theo trades their investigator credentials to smugglers for passage to the enemy capital, planning to deliver the key to both governments simultaneously. A betrayal by the smuggler captain costs them the physical archives; only the key and Ilsa's testimony remain. POV: Theo. Beat: loss stripping the mission to its irreducible core — one person, one truth.

chapters.title: The Room Where the War Was Written
chapters.summary: Theo infiltrates the Consortium's neutral arbitration station, where the original unedited files are stored, and finds Ilsa alive in holding. Together they access the raw footage: the atrocity was staged by contractors on both sides, with Consortium sign-off — signed by Theo's own mentor. POV: alternating. Beat: fury and grief fused into clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: With enforcers breaching the station and the ceasefire hours from expiring, Theo hijacks the arbitration station's all-band transmitter and streams the unedited files to both capitals at once. Wren arrives, weapon drawn, and in the end chooses not to fire — instead reading the broadcast aloud over open channels. POV: Theo. Beat: climax; sacrifice made public, loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Gravity Again
chapters.summary: Weeks later, both worlds reopen diplomatic channels, and the Consortium dissolves its enforcement arm under investigation. Theo, stripped of license but unrepentant, takes work verifying wrecks for grieving families; Ilsa sails home under her own name at last. The final beat is quiet restoration: gravity restored, records honest, and two voices answering across the silence. POV: Theo, closing letter format.
